findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — The attendee rows are committed before the calendar update, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but unsynced and a retry rejects them as existing.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — The server does not deduplicate the submitted guest list, allowing direct callers to create duplicate attendee records and duplicate notifications.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — Email delivery failures are swallowed, causing the mutation to report success although the newly added guests may never be notified.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any authenticated attendee can add arbitrary email addresses to a booking and receive its calendar/video details without organizer approval.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — The blacklist is lowercased but submitted guest addresses are not, allowing case-variant addresses to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — The attendee rows are committed before the calendar update, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but unsynced and a retry rejects them as existing.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, the flow is: 1) prisma.booking.update to add attendees (line 92-106), 2) eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees (line 161), 3) sendAddGuestsEmails (line 163). If updateCalendarAttendees fails, the attendees are already persisted in the database. On retry, uniqueGuests filtering (lines 68-72) would filter out already-added guests since they now exist in booking.attendees, causing the 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error if all guests were already added. This is a real atomicity/consistency issue where database and calendar can get out of sync, and retries would fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — Email delivery failures are swallowed, causing the mutation to report success although the newly added guests may never be notified.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts lines 163-168, the sendAddGuestsEmails call is wrapped in a try-catch that catches errors and only logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' to console, then continues to return { message: 'Guests added' }. This means if email delivery fails, the mutation still reports success to the user. However, the database update (adding guests to attendees) and calendar update have already succeeded at this point. The guests ARE added to the booking - they just might not receive notification emails. This is a design choice that prioritizes the core operation (adding guests) over email notification. The finding claims guests 'may never be notified' which is accurate for the email case, but the operation itself succeeded. This is a real issue - silent email failures mean users think everything worked when notifications failed, and there's no way to know or retry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any authenticated attendee can add arbitrary email addresses to a booking and receive its calendar/video details without organizer approval.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts, the authorization check at lines 47-53 verifies that the user is either: (1) a team admin/owner, (2) the organizer, or (3) an attendee of the booking. The finding claims 'any authenticated attendee can add arbitrary email addresses'. This is actually by design - attendees being able to add guests is a common feature in calendar systems. However, the finding raises a valid security concern: an attendee can add any email address as a guest, and those new guests will receive the full booking details including video call links (via AttendeeScheduledEmail sent to new guests at line 166). This could be a privacy/security issue if the organizer doesn't want attendees to be able to invite arbitrary third parties. The code doesn't check if the event type allows guests or if there's a guest limit. This is a real authorization gap - attendees having the same power as organizers to add guests without approval is a security concern.
